There have been a few things that have got me to write this reveiw.

When i got my babys birth certificate, i took it straight to the drs to verify him being registered. He got poorly 2 weeks later, at 5 weeks old. It was terrifying. I called for someone to check him. As I knew something was off.

They still had not put him on the system, the lady was on annual leave. So told me to call 111 as they couldnt see him. 111 sent me to A&E. He had a minor viral infection and the weather being hot. He had a creeping temp, breathing fast and deep, mottled skin. A&E and 111 where amazing with the care and understanding. After 6hrs was sent home but to take him straight back if his breathing or temp went up.

Recently.

5 months old, he had a cold and was congested for 2 weeks. Then sunday developed a cough and phlegm. I took him drs the monday. Got prescribed antibiotics and eye drops. Got told to buy piriton, calpol and nurofen.

Started antibiotics monday evening. At bath i noticed two big red blotches and spotty all over his belly. Tuesday morning he had spots on one of his cheeks too.

Tuesday i called drs to prescribe pirtion (Help open his airways of a night) as i could not buy it over the counter my baby is under 1, i picked it up that day.

I then called 111 about the reaction, She told me shes sending my information & the call details to the drs. To call them and get a call back or appointment to be seen. I was not to give anymore medicine till his been seen. I called the drs and they gave me a call back at 1.30 as i could not have an apointment.

Whilst i was waiting i went to the pharmacy to pick up piriton. I showed photos to the DR there. As he was due antibiotics soon. She asked if anyone in my family was alergic to peniciling and it was likely he was too.

The drs called me back, i was reassured it wasnt a reaction to the medication or raspberrys on his belly from my partner who got a coldsore the day after. It was just being unwell.

Wednesday evening his breathing became wheezy along with the other symptoms. We went to A&E. My baby is in fact allergic to peniciling and has broncilitis, did not have conjunctivitis, just watery eyes from the cough. I stopped medicine and kept an eye on him. Just a little piriton for his reaction. Thank you for your message and for sharing your concerns. The move to a total triage system is not a choice by the practice but a mandatory requirement set by the government. This means all appointment requests must first be triaged by a clinician, who will then direct patients to the most appropriate type of care.

We understand this is a change from how things have worked in the past, but the aim is to ensure patients are seen in the right place and at the right time. Vulnerable patients and those who need continuity of care will continue to be supported. Patients with no access to the internet, or a smart phone can still continue to contact reception by calling or walking in. The reception will help these patients to complete the request and submit these requests on their behalf. For further information you can contact the reception, we'll be happy to explain the total triage process further. 

Thank you also for your kind wishes to Dr Chajed, which we will pass on.
